mainEntity.name: What is the difference between replastering and resurfacing a pool?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replastering refers to applying a new layer of plaster to the interior surface of a concrete pool. This is typically done when the existing plaster shows signs of wear, staining, or minor cracking. Resurfacing is a broader term that encompasses replastering but can also refer to applying other finishes, such as pebble tec, quartz, or tile, which offer different aesthetics and durability. While replastering is a form of resurfacing, resurfacing provides more diverse material options to choose from, often enhancing both look and longevity.
